sourceKind: statute for the mirror-code territories; a secondary summary for Puerto Rico; American Samoa's rate is an estimate from its adopted code

source.title: 48 U.S.C. § 1421i (Organic Act of Guam § 31): the Internal Revenue Code of the United States applies in Guam as the Guam Territorial Income Tax, so a corporation pays the section 11 rate (26 U.S.C. 11(b), 21 percent) to Guam in place of the United States; IRS Publication 570

48 U.S.C. § 1397 (the Internal Revenue Code applies in the Virgin Islands as the Virgin Islands income tax, so a corporation pays the section 11 rate, 21 percent, to the territory in place of the United States); V.I. BIR Revenue Ruling 2025-1223-1; IRS Publication 570
Commonwealth Code 4 CMC §§ 1204, 1206, 1708 (the Northern Mariana Islands territorial income tax mirrors the Internal Revenue Code; cnmilaw.gov notes content may be out of date); IRS Publication 570

US-AS.system: own code based on a frozen IRC
US-AS.estimatedFrom: A.S.C.A. § 11.0403 adopts the income tax rules of the United States in effect on December 31, 2000, which for a corporation is the section 11 schedule of that date (15 percent rising to a top rate of 35 percent); the territory's own current corporate rate table was not read.

source.title: A.S.C.A. § 11.0403 and § 11.0503 (American Samoa Bar Association code annotated); IRS Publication 570
